text: EMERGENCY PULMONARY CT ANGIOGRAPHY EXAMINATION CLINICAL INFORMATION: TECHNIQUE: In emergency conditions, 1 mm thick sections were obtained after intravenous contrast agent injection, and evaluation was performed in 3 planes from MPR images. 100 ml of nonionic contrast agent was used for the examination. FINDINGS: Respiratory motion artifacts reduced the diagnostic value of the examination. The trachea and both main bronchi were of normal width. No filling defect consistent with PTE was detected in either main pulmonary artery or its visible proximal branches. Heart dimensions were increased. An effusion measuring 10 mm at its thickest point was observed in the pericardial area. No pathologically enlarged lymph nodes were detected in the mediastinum or both hilum. A mosaic attenuation pattern is observed in both lungs. There is a suspicious appearance for a peripherally located ground-glass opacity in the posterior upper lobe of the right lung. However, a clear distinction cannot be made in terms of mosaic attenuation patterns. Clinical evaluation is recommended. Increased interlobular septal thickness is present in both lungs. Left lung ventilation is reduced. A smear-like effusion, measuring approximately 3 mm at its thickest point, was observed in the right hemithorax. Increased thickness of extrapleural fat tissue is observed in both hemithoraxes.

EMERGENCY PULMONARY CT ANGIOGRAPHY EXAMINATION CLINICAL INFORMATION: STABBING PAIN ON THE LEFT SIDE TECHNIQUE: Intravenous contrast agent was injected in an emergency setting, 1 mm thick sections were obtained, and evaluation was performed in 3 planes using MPR images. 100 ml of nonionic contrast agent was used for the examination. FINDINGS: The trachea and both main bronchi are of normal width. The pulmonary trunk diameter is 39 mm, which is increased. There is a sudden decrease in caliber in the proximal segmental branch of the pulmonary artery going to the anterior segment of the upper lobe of the left lung, raising suspicion of PTE. Evaluation of the patient in conjunction with clinical and laboratory findings is recommended. Heart dimensions are within normal limits. No pathologically enlarged lymph nodes were detected in the mediastinum or both hilum. Cystic and tubular bronchiectasis with scattered mucus impactions were noted in both lungs, more prominent on the right. In both lungs, more prominent on the left, areas of tree-in-bud and acinar nodular infiltration were observed in the subpleural and peribronchial spaces. Pleural effusion, reaching a depth of 2 cm at the level of the right lung, and areas of passive atelectasis adjacent to the effusion were observed in both lungs, with the effusion extending into the fissures. Pleural thickening was also present in both lungs. The findings in the lung parenchyma are largely similar to those in the previous CT scan.

EMERGENCY NON-CONTRAST THORACIC CT EXAMINATION CLINICAL INFORMATION: COVID? TECHNIQUE: 2 mm thick sections were obtained under emergency conditions without intravenous contrast administration. FINDINGS: Due to the lack of IV contrast, optimal evaluation of the heart chambers, mediastinal vascular structures, and lymph nodes could not be performed. Heart dimensions are normal. Densities of secretions extending from the distal sections of both main bronchi to the lower lobar bronchus were observed. Both lower lung lobes appeared almost completely consolidated-collapsed. Singular fibroatelectatic changes were observed in the lingular segment of both lungs and in the middle lobe of the right lung. A pleural effusion measuring 15 mm in thickness at its thickest point and extending to the apex was detected in the right hemithorax. A pleural effusion measuring 20 mm in thickness is present in the left hemithorax.
